name: Marina di Carrara
title: Marina di Carrara UTM | Heavy-Lift & Marble Carrier Gauging
description: Thickness measurement at Marina di Carrara for heavy-lift, multipurpose and bulk ships loading marble and project cargo: holds, tank tops and hatch covers.
h1: Marina di Carrara: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Heavy-Lift and Marble Cargo Ships
intro: Marina di Carrara is the Tuscan port that ships marble blocks, slabs and heavy project cargo from the Apuan quarries. The ships that load here put unusual stress on hold structure and tank tops, and they often stay long enough for a planned set of readings. Atlantis NDT sends ultrasonic gauging technicians from India to the vessel, and fits the work to the loading plan and the surveyor's requirements.

highlights.h: Marble loads that punish tank tops
highlights.p: Dense blocks are lowered onto tank tops and tween decks with limited cushioning. Readings taken between cargoes show how much plating and how many frames have worn, and whether a repair belongs in the next yard period.

Ships carrying large industrial equipment use the quays here as well. Deck strengthening, lashing points, crane pedestals and heavy-lift gear foundations all call for ultrasonic readings and crack detection at known fatigue spots.
Stowing stone cargo is careful, deliberate work. Ships often stay alongside longer than a container call, which leaves room to gauge holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks in a planned order.

port.h: Marina di Carrara: a stone port on an open Tuscan coast
p: Marina di Carrara lies on the Tuscan coast between La Spezia and Viareggio, below the marble quarries of the Apuan Alps. It forms part of the eastern Ligurian Sea port system, run by the same authority as La Spezia, and its role is quite different from the container gateway to the north. The port grew up to ship the stone that quarries in the surrounding hills still cut today: raw blocks, slabs, tiles and processed stone, plus heavy machinery made in the region for export.

The ships that load here are mostly multipurpose vessels, heavy-lift ships, general cargo ships and small bulk carriers. Their holds are fitted for stone, with tween decks and reinforced tank tops, and many carry their own cranes. Marble blocks are heavy and awkward, and loading calls for careful stowage and lashing. Project cargo adds large machines for the energy industry and other sectors, some moved on heavy-lift ships that arrive with a defined slot and a tight plan. Cruise calls are rare, and tanker traffic is minimal. The port is a working cargo harbour with a quiet pace compared with its neighbours.

Unlike La Spezia, Marina di Carrara has no sheltered gulf. The port faces the open sea, and a swell from the south-west can run into the entrance and make anchorage work uncomfortable. Ships waiting for a berth usually lie off the coast, and launch transfers depend on the sea state. The dwell time for stone ships is longer than for liner services, which helps, but weather is the planning risk. Because yard facilities for large merchant dockings are limited locally, owners often send ships to Genoa, La Spezia or elsewhere for a full survey, and gauging at Carrara supports that decision.

facilities.h: Quays, holds and offshore waiting areas at Marina di Carrara
p: Gauging at the quay concentrates on the structures that stone cargo attacks. After discharge or before loading, holds are empty and accessible, and tank tops, tween deck plating, frames and hatch coamings can be measured. Hatch covers, crane pedestals and lashing points on deck complete the picture, with magnetic particle testing at welds that carry concentrated loads. Ballast tanks that the chief officer can ventilate and release for entry are measured alongside, and deck piping and fire mains can be checked at the same visit.

Because the ships are often geared, ultrasonic readings on cranes and their foundations are common, with the owner's permission and the crane maker's drawings. Heavy-lift ships bring a different set of questions about deck strength and lashing arrangements. For ships at anchor off the coast, the agent arranges a launch, and weather decides whether the plan holds. When a full renewal or intermediate survey is due, the practical route is a docking at a larger yard along the coast, and Carrara serves as the place to size the work in advance. The technicians travel with their own equipment and do not need shore gauges or staging from the port.
list: Marble and general cargo quays: hold, tank top, tween deck and hatch coaming gauging on multipurpose ships between cargoes
Heavy-lift berths: deck structure, crane pedestal and lashing point gauging with crack detection at highly loaded welds
Ballast tank gauging alongside where the officers can release spaces for entry
Deck piping, fire main and sea-water line gauging during the loading stay
Offshore waiting area: pre-purchase and charter condition gauging by launch, subject to swell
Yards in La Spezia and Genoa: where readings from Carrara feed the steel estimate for a docking

context.h: Port state control and the logic of stone and project cargo
p: Italy belongs to the Paris MoU, and port state control on foreign ships at Marina di Carrara is carried out by the Guardia Costiera, the Italian Coast Guard, through the local port office. Cargo ships with worn holds and corroded hatch covers can be flagged, and wasted structure around cargo handling gear can lead to deficiencies. The Mediterranean SOx emission control area applies here, so ships burn low-sulphur fuel or run scrubbers, and scrubber piping on larger vessels is gauged alongside the structure.

The commercial drivers differ from a container port. Stone shipping is cyclical, and multipurpose ships move between cargoes, so charterers and buyers often ask for condition reports before fixing a ship or taking one on hire. Heavy-lift ships are valued for their gear and deck, and a gauging record of the deck and foundations supports a sale or charter. EU carbon rules, namely the Emissions Trading System since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025, add pressure on older small tonnage, which is common in the multipurpose trade. Ships calling at EU ports also need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the Ship Recycling Regulation, and a clear structural record helps owners plan the last years of a ship's life.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Marina di Carrara
jobs.p: Marina di Carrara jobs are about structure that carries heavy loads. Enquiries come from owners and managers of multipurpose and heavy-lift ships, from charterers who want an independent condition record and from buyers. The loading plan sets the window, so we agree spaces, permits and report format before the team travels. Typical requests include:
list: Tank top and tween deck gauging in the holds of a multipurpose ship between marble cargoes, mapping wastage under the points where blocks are landed.
Hatch cover and coaming gauging on a heavy-lift ship, with magnetic particle testing at welded details around crane pedestals.
Ballast tank and deck piping gauging alongside, closing out a surveyor's note before an annual survey.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a small bulk carrier lying off the coast, limited to spaces the crew can make safe.
Pre-docking readings across holds and tanks, so a yard in La Spezia or Genoa can estimate steel work before the ship arrives.

logistics: Pisa Galileo Galilei Airport is the nearest main airport, and Genoa and Florence are alternatives for longer-haul links. Technicians from India usually connect through a European hub and complete the journey by road or rail. Italy is within the Schengen area, so Schengen visas are needed and travel is booked once they are issued. Quay access, ISPS passes and launches for ships waiting offshore are arranged through the ship's agent, and our team brings its own equipment.
vessels: Occasional small cruise or expedition ships

faqs.q: Why gauge tank tops on a ship that loads marble?
faqs.a: Marble blocks are very dense and are landed on the tank top with limited cushioning, which wears plating and frames faster than lighter cargoes. Ultrasonic readings between cargoes show how much steel remains and help the owner plan a repair period before findings turn into survey conditions.

faqs.q: Can you gauge crane foundations and lashing points?
faqs.a: Yes, within the owner's brief. We measure plating around crane pedestals, lashing points and strengthened deck areas, and use magnetic particle testing at welds with high local loads. We ask for relevant drawings in advance so that readings are taken at the right positions.

faqs.q: Does swell affect work at Marina di Carrara?
faqs.a: It can, mostly at the anchorage. The port faces the open sea, so a south-westerly swell may stop launch boarding. At the quay, work continues in most conditions. For ships waiting offshore we build a spare day into the plan.

faqs.q: Where would a ship dock for a full survey after gauging at Carrara?
faqs.a: That is for the owner and class to decide. Yards in La Spezia, Genoa and elsewhere on the Mediterranean are the usual options. The readings from Carrara serve as an early steel estimate, and the same technicians can join the ship at the yard to finish the survey.
